specification.problem: Simon's Problem: given a black box f:{0,1}^n->{0,1}^n with f(x)=f(y) iff y=x or y=x XOR s, find the hidden period s. Scoped to the logical two-qubit version (n=2), which the abstract says was realized one-way on a five-qubit cluster state via single-qubit measurement basis choices.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Standard circuit-model Simon algorithm for n=2 with one assumed representative oracle (s=11, f(00)=f(11), f(01)=f(10)), plus classical postprocessing of the orthogonality equations. Outside scope: the five-qubit cluster-state construction, measurement angles per function, photonic implementation, experimental fidelity, and the n-qubit resource analysis, none of which can be reconstructed from the abstract.

symbols.meaning: number of logical input qubits (n=2 here)

equations.label: Output distribution after Hadamards
equations.description: Measuring the input register after H^{\otimes n} yields z uniformly from those orthogonal to s
equations.justification: Standard Simon analysis, not evidence from the abstract.

equations.label: Instance outcomes
equations.description: For s=11, the allowed z satisfy z\cdot s=0 mod 2
equations.justification: Follows from eq_3 and the assumed instance eq_4.

steps.description: Apply H on both input qubits to form the uniform superposition.
Apply H on the input qubits and measure them in the computational basis.
Repeat until the nonzero outcomes determine s via z·s=0.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the 2 input qubits (circuit model); the cluster-state version uses single-qubit measurements in chosen bases, not specified in the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Collect the nonzero z values and solve z·s=0 mod 2 for nonzero s; for n=2, s=11 follows from the single outcome z=11.
assumptions: Circuit-model reconstruction is used as a proxy for the one-way implementation
The instance s=11 is chosen by me, not from the abstract
